security_audit.summary: Most shell-related alerts are documentation references to tool names, test macros, or code fences. The skill still instructs agents to run the local ./bin/mage REPL command as a fallback. The parent-directory includes are confirmed high risk because they pull unaudited shared files outside the packaged skill.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the ../ shared references with files packaged inside the skill, or inline the required instructions for audit.
Require user confirmation before running ./bin/mage, and document the exact trusted repository context.

content.user_title: Build Clojure Features with REPL Guidance
content.value_statement: Clojure changes can fail late when functions are composed before they are tested. This skill guides REPL-first development, evaluation, refactoring, and docstring cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Prefers clojure-mcp evaluation and editing tools when available.
Guides bottom-up REPL development for small functions.
Shows when to use the Metabase mage REPL fallback.
Explains how to move validated REPL work into source files.
Defines caller-focused docstring expectations for Clojure code.
Calls for readability checks after Clojure edits.
limitations: The package does not include referenced shared workflow files.
Full workflow depends on a trusted Metabase checkout.
Shell fallback requires local mage command availability.
It does not provide automated tests or scripts.

use_cases.title: Implement a Metabase Clojure change
use_cases.description: Plan small functions, evaluate them in the REPL, and compose them only after validation.

use_cases.title: Refactor ClojureScript safely
use_cases.description: Break a refactor into focused edits and verify each namespace before continuing.

use_cases.title: Review docstrings before release
use_cases.description: Move implementation details out of docstrings and keep caller-facing contracts clear.

prompt_templates.title: Start a REPL Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the clojure-write workflow to plan a small Clojure change. Prefer clojure-mcp tools and list the first REPL checks.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Namespace
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me evaluate this namespace after my edit. Identify the smallest functions to test before composing larger behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor With Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide a Clojure refactor using bottom-up REPL checks. Tell me what to verify before moving each change into tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Large Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this Metabase Clojure change into safe stages. Include REPL validation, readability checks, and docstring review.

output_examples.input: I need a new Clojure helper for database connection validation.
output: Identify the smallest pure helper first.
Evaluate the namespace before composing larger behavior.
Move verified logic into the source file and add a focused test.

output_examples.input: I changed a ClojureScript namespace and want a review plan.
output: Check that the namespace loads after the edit.
Run focused REPL trials for changed functions.
Confirm docstrings describe caller contracts, not implementation history.

output_examples.input: I found a long docstring with implementation notes.
output: Keep caller requirements in the docstring.
Move useful implementation context near the relevant body line.
Delete only text that restates obvious behavior.

best_practices: Use clojure-mcp evaluation and editing tools before shell fallback.
Evaluate each namespace after every Clojure change.
Keep docstrings focused on caller contracts and invariants.
anti_patterns: Running fallback shell commands before checking MCP tool availability.
Writing multi-paragraph docstrings without user confirmation.
Composing untested REPL experiments directly into larger code.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code for Clojure development guidance.

faq.question: Does it run code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow instructions for agents and users to apply.

faq.question: Is it specific to Metabase?
faq.answer: Yes. It references Metabase commands and conventions, though many Clojure practices are general.

faq.question: Does it include shared style files?
faq.answer: No. The package references shared parent files that are not included in this audit.

faq.question: Can it help with docstrings?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains caller-focused docstrings and where implementation notes should live.

faq.question: What should users verify before use?
faq.answer: Confirm the repository is trusted and review any shell command before execution.
